name: Detecting Network-Layer Attacks with Splunk & Zeek/Bro Logs
command: index="cobaltstrike_beacon" sourcetype="bro:http:json" | sort 0 _time | streamstats current=f last(_time) as prevtime by src, dest, dest_port | eval timedelta = _time - prevtime | eventstats avg(timedelta) as avg, count as total by src, dest, dest_port | eval upper=avg*1.1 | eval lower=avg*0.9 | where timedelta > lower AND timedelta < upper | stats count, values(avg) as TimeInterval by src, dest, dest_port, total | eval prcnt = (count/total)*100 | where prcnt > 90 AND total > 10
description: Splunk SPL queries for detecting network-layer attacks using Zeek/Bro logs. Covers: RDP brute force (bro:rdp:json count>30 in 5m), C2 beaconing (bro:http:json streamstats timedelta avg±10% prcnt>90), Nmap port scanning (bro:conn:json orig_bytes=0 dc(dest_port)>=3 in 5m), Kerberos brute force (bro:kerberos:json error_msg!=KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED count>30), Kerberoasting (bro:kerberos:json TGS rc4-hmac forwardable renewable), Golden Tickets (bro:kerberos:json TGS-only unique_request_types==1), Cobalt Strike PSExec (bro:smb_files:json FILE_OPEN *.exe/dll/bat on c$/ADMIN$), Zerologon (bro:dce_rpc:json netlogon unique_operations>=2 count>100), HTTP exfiltration (bro:http:json POST sum(request_body_len)/1024/1024), DNS exfiltration (bro:dns:json len_query>=40 req_by_day>60), Ransomware (bro:smb_files:json FILE_OPEN+FILE_RENAME>100 in 5m; extension change detection).
source: CDSA Module 14: Detecting Windows Attacks with Splunk
notes:
=== MODULE CONTEXT ===
Zeek (formerly Bro) generates structured JSON logs from pcap/live traffic.
Splunk sourcetypes used:
  bro:rdp:json     → RDP session metadata
  bro:http:json    → HTTP request/response metadata (URI, method, bytes, host)
  bro:conn:json    → connection summaries (bytes, duration, ports, flags)
  bro:kerberos:json → Kerberos AS/TGS request metadata (client, cipher, success, error_msg)
  bro:smb_files:json → SMB file operations (action, name, path, size, timestamps)
  bro:dce_rpc:json  → DCE/RPC call metadata (endpoint, operation)
  bro:dns:json      → DNS query/response (query, qtype, answers, rtt)

Lab setup: target system has Splunk + Zeek; log files in /home/htb-student/module_files/
Connect: xfreerdp /u:htb-student /p:'HTB_@cademy_stdnt!' /v:[Target IP] /dynamic-resolution

=== SECTION 12 — RDP BRUTE FORCE ===
index="rdp_bruteforce" sourcetype="bro:rdp:json"
  | bin _time span=5m
  | stats count values(cookie) by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h
  | where count>30
Detects: >30 RDP connections from same source to same dest in 5 minutes = brute force
Zeek RDP fields: id.orig_h (src IP), id.resp_h (dest IP), cookie (RDP routing token = username)
Note: Also applicable to SSH brute force with adjusted sourcetype and fields

=== SECTION 13 — C2 BEACONING DETECTION ===
index="cobaltstrike_beacon" sourcetype="bro:http:json"
  | sort 0 _time
  | streamstats current=f last(_time) as prevtime by src, dest, dest_port
  | eval timedelta = _time - prevtime
  | eventstats avg(timedelta) as avg, count as total by src, dest, dest_port
  | eval upper=avg*1.1
  | eval lower=avg*0.9
  | where timedelta > lower AND timedelta < upper
  | stats count, values(avg) as TimeInterval by src, dest, dest_port, total
  | eval prcnt = (count/total)*100
  | where prcnt > 90 AND total > 10
Logic: C2 beacons at consistent intervals (jitter ≤10%)
  streamstats: computes time since last event per src/dest/port pair
  timedelta = seconds between consecutive HTTP requests
  avg±10% window: events within 10% of average interval = regular interval
  prcnt>90: >90% of requests within the interval window = highly regular = beacon
  total>10: at least 10 events = established pattern (not random)
Typical beacon config (Cobalt Strike): SleepTime=60s, Jitter=0% → all requests ~60s apart

=== SECTION 14 — NMAP PORT SCANNING ===
index="cobaltstrike_beacon" sourcetype="bro:conn:json" orig_bytes=0
  dest_ip IN (192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 10.0.0.0/8)
  | bin span=5m _time
  | stats dc(dest_port) as num_dest_port by _time, src_ip, dest_ip
  | where num_dest_port >= 3
Logic: Port scans send SYN with no data (orig_bytes=0); target internal RFC1918 ranges
  dc(dest_port) = distinct destination ports per src→dest pair in 5 min
  >=3 distinct ports in 5 minutes = scanning behavior
Note: TCP SYN scan: RST from closed ports → orig_bytes=0 is the key indicator
  Nmap SYN scan (-sS): no application data sent in probe packets

=== SECTION 15 — KERBEROS BRUTE FORCE ===
index="kerberos_bruteforce" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json"
  error_msg!=KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED success="false" request_type=AS
  | bin _time span=5m
  | stats count dc(client) as "Unique users" values(error_msg) as "Error messages"
      by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h
  | where count>30
Logic: Kerberos brute force = many AS-REQ (TGT requests) with failures
  request_type=AS: only authentication requests (TGT), not TGS
  error_msg!=KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED: exclude normal pre-auth prompt (not an error)
  success="false": only failed authentication
  count>30 in 5m: high-volume failure rate = brute force
Common Kerberos error codes:
  KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED: normal response requesting timestamp (not a failure)
  KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN: invalid username
  KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED: wrong password
  KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED: account disabled/locked

=== SECTION 16 — KERBEROASTING (Zeek) ===
index="sharphound" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json"
  request_type=TGS cipher="rc4-hmac" forwardable="true" renewable="true"
  | table _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, request_type, cipher, forwardable, renewable, client, service
Logic: Kerberoasting requests TGS for service accounts using RC4-HMAC encryption
  rc4-hmac: weaker encryption, required for offline cracking with Hashcat/JtR
  forwardable=true + renewable=true: ticket flags set by attack tools (Rubeus/Impacket)
  AES-encrypted tickets (aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96) are much harder to crack
False positive reduction: legitimate access uses AES or has matching service connection
Note: Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17 in EID 4769 = RC4-HMAC; same indicator in Windows event logs

=== SECTION 17 — GOLDEN TICKET DETECTION (Zeek) ===
index="golden_ticket_attack" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json"
  | where client!="-"
  | bin _time span=1m
  | stats values(client), values(request_type) as request_types, dc(request_type) as unique_request_types
      by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h
  | where request_types=="TGS" AND unique_request_types==1
Logic: Golden Ticket = attacker has forged TGT, imports it, then requests TGS for service
  Normal: client sends AS-REQ (TGT) → then TGS-REQ (service ticket) = both AS and TGS
  Golden Ticket: only TGS seen at DC (TGT was forged offline, never sent to DC)
  unique_request_types==1 AND request_types=="TGS": only TGS requests, no AS requests
  Combined with PtT detection (Section 6): same host has TGS without prior TGT on wire

=== SECTION 18 — COBALT STRIKE PSExec (SMB) ===
index="cobalt_strike_psexec" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json"
  action="SMB::FILE_OPEN"
  name IN ("*.exe", "*.dll", "*.bat")
  path IN ("*\\c$", "*\\ADMIN$")
  size>0
Logic: PSExec drops a service binary to admin shares (C$ or ADMIN$) then executes it
  SMB::FILE_OPEN: Zeek records when SMB client opens/creates a file on a share
  name IN *.exe/dll/bat: executable/script upload
  path IN c$/ADMIN$: admin shares = only accessible to administrators
  size>0: actual file being written (not just a directory access)
Cobalt Strike PSExec IOCs:
  Service binary: short random hex name (e.g., be5312f.exe)
  Share: ADMIN$ or C$\Windows
  Creates service → executes payload → deletes service binary

=== SECTION 19 — ZEROLOGON (CVE-2020-1472) ===
index="zerologon" endpoint="netlogon" sourcetype="bro:dce_rpc:json"
  | bin _time span=1m
  | where operation == "NetrServerReqChallenge"
      OR operation == "NetrServerAuthenticate3"
      OR operation == "NetrServerPasswordSet2"
  | stats count values(operation) as operation_values dc(operation) as unique_operations
      by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h
  | where unique_operations >= 2 AND count>100
Logic: Zerologon exploits Netlogon protocol (MS-NRPC) — sets DC machine account password to empty
  NetrServerReqChallenge: challenge exchange (attacker sends ~256 attempts with zeroed ClientChallenge)
  NetrServerAuthenticate3: authentication response
  NetrServerPasswordSet2: set new computer password (attacker sets it to empty/known)
  count>100 in 1min: requires many failed attempts to exploit the AES-CFB8 IV=0 vulnerability
  unique_operations>=2: multiple distinct Netlogon RPC operations = active exploit sequence
CVE-2020-1472: exploits AES-CFB8 mode — zero IV means 1/256 chance each auth succeeds

=== SECTION 20 — HTTP DATA EXFILTRATION ===
index="cobaltstrike_exfiltration_http" sourcetype="bro:http:json" method=POST
  | stats sum(request_body_len) as TotalBytes by src, dest, dest_port
  | eval TotalBytes = TotalBytes/1024/1024
Detects: large volumes of data exfiltrated via HTTP POST requests
  request_body_len: bytes in the HTTP request body (outbound data)
  sum across all POSTs per src→dest pair
  eval to MB for readability
Cobalt Strike HTTP POST exfil: default POST to /submit.php or configured URI
Threshold guidance: alert on >X MB per hour per src/dest depending on baseline
Also check: response_body_len (C2 command downloads inbound)

=== SECTION 21 — DNS DATA EXFILTRATION ===
index=dns_exf sourcetype="bro:dns:json"
  | eval len_query=len(query)
  | search len_query>=40 AND query!="*.ip6.arpa*" AND query!="*amazonaws.com*"
      AND query!="*._googlecast.*" AND query!="_ldap.*"
  | bin _time span=24h
  | stats count(query) as req_by_day by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h
  | where req_by_day>60
  | table _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, req_by_day
Logic: DNS exfil encodes data in subdomain labels of controlled domain (e.g., <base64data>.attacker.com)
  len_query>=40: exfil queries encode data → subdomains are long (legitimate queries typically shorter)
  Exclusions: ptr lookups, AWS CDN, Chromecast, LDAP SRV records (legitimate long queries)
  req_by_day>60: >60 long DNS queries/day to same resolver = sustained exfiltration
Tools: DNScat2, iodine, custom scripts
Note: Also look for queries to the same second-level domain at high frequency

=== SECTION 22 — RANSOMWARE DETECTION ===

--- Excessive File Overwriting (Sodinokibi/REvil pattern) ---
index="ransomware_open_rename_sodinokibi" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json"
  | where action IN ("SMB::FILE_OPEN", "SMB::FILE_RENAME")
  | bin _time span=5m
  | stats count by _time, source, action
  | where count>30
  | stats sum(count) as count values(action) dc(action) as uniq_actions by _time, source
  | where uniq_actions==2 AND count>100
Logic: Ransomware opens files (read plaintext) → renames to encrypted version
  uniq_actions==2: BOTH FILE_OPEN and FILE_RENAME actions present
  count>100 in 5 min: bulk encryption volume
  source: the SMB server share being targeted

--- New File Extension Ransomware (CTBLocker/extension-change pattern) ---
index="ransomware_new_file_extension_ctbl_ocker" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json"
  action="SMB::FILE_RENAME"
  | bin _time span=5m
  | rex field="name" "\.(?<new_file_name_extension>[^\.]*$)"
  | rex field="prev_name" "\.(?<old_file_name_extension>[^\.]*$)"
  | stats count by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_p, name, source,
      old_file_name_extension, new_file_name_extension
  | where new_file_name_extension!=old_file_name_extension
  | stats count by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_p, source, new_file_name_extension
  | where count>20
  | sort -count
Logic: File renames where extension changes = encryption in progress
  rex extracts extension from file name and prev_name fields
  where new!=old: extension actually changed (not just a rename within same type)
  count>20 in 5 min: bulk extension changes = ransomware
  sort -count: highest activity first

=== ZEEK LOG FIELD REFERENCE ===
bro:rdp:json:
  id.orig_h/id.resp_h: src/dst IP | cookie: RDP routing token (often encodes username)

bro:http:json:
  src/dest: IPs | dest_port | method: GET/POST/PUT | uri | request_body_len | response_body_len
  host: HTTP Host header | user_agent | status_code | referrer

bro:conn:json:
  id.orig_h/id.resp_h/id.orig_p/id.resp_p: IPs and ports
  proto: tcp/udp | service: detected application
  orig_bytes/resp_bytes: bytes sent each direction (0 = no payload = port scan SYN)
  duration: connection duration

bro:kerberos:json:
  client: client principal (user@REALM) | service: service principal
  request_type: AS (TGT) or TGS (service ticket)
  success: true/false | error_msg: KDC error string
  cipher: encryption type (rc4-hmac, aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96)
  forwardable/renewable: ticket flags

bro:smb_files:json:
  action: SMB::FILE_OPEN, SMB::FILE_RENAME, SMB::FILE_DELETE, SMB::FILE_WRITE
  name: current filename | prev_name: original filename (rename operations)
  path: UNC share path (e.g., \\server\ADMIN$)
  size: file size in bytes
  id.orig_h/id.resp_h: client/server IPs

bro:dce_rpc:json:
  endpoint: RPC interface (e.g., netlogon, srvsvc, samr)
  operation: specific RPC function called
  id.orig_h/id.resp_h: client/server IPs

bro:dns:json:
  query: queried hostname | qtype_name: query type (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, etc.)
  id.orig_h/id.resp_h: client/resolver IPs
  answers: list of resolved values
  rtt: round-trip time

examples.label: Detect RDP brute force — >30 RDP connections in 5 minutes
examples.command: index="rdp_bruteforce" sourcetype="bro:rdp:json" | bin _time span=5m | stats count values(cookie) by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h | where count>30

examples.label: Detect C2 beaconing — consistent HTTP intervals with <10% jitter
examples.command: index="cobaltstrike_beacon" sourcetype="bro:http:json" | sort 0 _time | streamstats current=f last(_time) as prevtime by src, dest, dest_port | eval timedelta = _time - prevtime | eventstats avg(timedelta) as avg, count as total by src, dest, dest_port | eval upper=avg*1.1 | eval lower=avg*0.9 | where timedelta > lower AND timedelta < upper | stats count, values(avg) as TimeInterval by src, dest, dest_port, total | eval prcnt = (count/total)*100 | where prcnt > 90 AND total > 10

examples.label: Detect Nmap port scanning — zero-byte connections to 3+ ports in 5 min
examples.command: index="cobaltstrike_beacon" sourcetype="bro:conn:json" orig_bytes=0 dest_ip IN (192.168.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 10.0.0.0/8) | bin span=5m _time | stats dc(dest_port) as num_dest_port by _time, src_ip, dest_ip | where num_dest_port >= 3

examples.label: Detect Kerberos brute force — >30 AS failures in 5 minutes
examples.command: index="kerberos_bruteforce" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json" error_msg!=KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED success="false" request_type=AS | bin _time span=5m | stats count dc(client) as "Unique users" values(error_msg) as "Error messages" by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h | where count>30

examples.label: Detect Kerberoasting — TGS requests using RC4-HMAC encryption
examples.command: index="sharphound" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json" request_type=TGS cipher="rc4-hmac" forwardable="true" renewable="true" | table _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, request_type, cipher, forwardable, renewable, client, service

examples.label: Detect Golden Ticket — TGS requests without any prior AS (TGT) requests
examples.command: index="golden_ticket_attack" sourcetype="bro:kerberos:json" | where client!="-" | bin _time span=1m | stats values(client), values(request_type) as request_types, dc(request_type) as unique_request_types by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h | where request_types=="TGS" AND unique_request_types==1

examples.label: Detect Cobalt Strike PSExec — executable dropped to admin shares via SMB
examples.command: index="cobalt_strike_psexec" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json" action="SMB::FILE_OPEN" name IN ("*.exe", "*.dll", "*.bat") path IN ("*\\c$", "*\\ADMIN$") size>0

examples.label: Detect Zerologon — bulk Netlogon RPC calls with multiple distinct operations
examples.command: index="zerologon" endpoint="netlogon" sourcetype="bro:dce_rpc:json" | bin _time span=1m | where operation == "NetrServerReqChallenge" OR operation == "NetrServerAuthenticate3" OR operation == "NetrServerPasswordSet2" | stats count values(operation) as operation_values dc(operation) as unique_operations by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h | where unique_operations >= 2 AND count>100

examples.label: Detect HTTP data exfiltration — large POST volume to single destination
examples.command: index="cobaltstrike_exfiltration_http" sourcetype="bro:http:json" method=POST | stats sum(request_body_len) as TotalBytes by src, dest, dest_port | eval TotalBytes = TotalBytes/1024/1024

examples.label: Detect DNS exfiltration — high frequency of long DNS queries per day
examples.command: index=dns_exf sourcetype="bro:dns:json" | eval len_query=len(query) | search len_query>=40 AND query!="*.ip6.arpa*" AND query!="*amazonaws.com*" AND query!="*._googlecast.*" AND query!="_ldap.*" | bin _time span=24h | stats count(query) as req_by_day by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h | where req_by_day>60 | table _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_h, req_by_day

examples.label: Detect ransomware — bulk FILE_OPEN + FILE_RENAME on same share in 5 minutes
examples.command: index="ransomware_open_rename_sodinokibi" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json" | where action IN ("SMB::FILE_OPEN", "SMB::FILE_RENAME") | bin _time span=5m | stats count by _time, source, action | where count>30 | stats sum(count) as count values(action) dc(action) as uniq_actions by _time, source | where uniq_actions==2 AND count>100

examples.label: Detect ransomware — file extension changes in bulk (>20 in 5 minutes)
examples.command: index="ransomware_new_file_extension_ctbl_ocker" sourcetype="bro:smb_files:json" action="SMB::FILE_RENAME" | bin _time span=5m | rex field="name" "\.(?<new_file_name_extension>[^\.]*$)" | rex field="prev_name" "\.(?<old_file_name_extension>[^\.]*$)" | stats count by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_p, name, source, old_file_name_extension, new_file_name_extension | where new_file_name_extension!=old_file_name_extension | stats count by _time, id.orig_h, id.resp_p, source, new_file_name_extension | where count>20 | sort -count
